description: Rhetorical scaffolding: the setups, reveals and fragments a model reaches for when it is performing insight rather than delivering one. Every feature here has a matching prose rule in the no-ai-slop skill.
baselineNote: All baselines are default_prior, reasoned from the skill's own guidance rather than measured. Run `aiwd calibrate` against a genre corpus before treating any z-score as a measurement.

features.explanation: Setup phrases that delay the point. Cut them and state the claim.
features.falsifiedBy: A calibrated baseline showing human expository prose opens this way at a comparable rate.

lexicon: this is the part most people skip
features.explanation: Flatters the writer as the lone expert. Cut the setup and let the claim stand alone.
features.falsifiedBy: A calibrated baseline for opinion or blog genres where this framing is conventional.

features.explanation: Staged questions and reveals. Drop the setup and make the point.
features.falsifiedBy: A calibrated baseline for spoken-register or marketing genres.

features.explanation: Noun phrase, colon, lowercase dramatic reveal. Rewrite as a plain sentence; keep colons for lists, labels and quotes.
features.falsifiedBy: A calibrated baseline showing the construction is common in edited human prose at this rate.

features.explanation: "Not a X. Not a Y. A Z." Say Z.
features.falsifiedBy: A calibrated baseline where anaphoric negation is a documented feature of the genre.

features.pattern: (?:^|[.!?]\s+)(?:that's it|that is it|that's the whole thing|full stop|period|end of story|simple as that|no more, no less)\s*[.!]
features.explanation: Punchy terminal fragments used for emphasis. Use complete sentences.
features.falsifiedBy: A calibrated baseline for conversational or column genres.

lexicon: in the end, it comes down to
features.explanation: The closing aphorism. Delete it and end on the clearest concrete sentence already present.
features.falsifiedBy: A calibrated baseline for essay or op-ed genres where a closing turn is conventional.
